subject: Private deployment evaluation & MAP proposal
messages:
From: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@enterpriseai.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Walker <tom.walker@enterpriseai.com>, procurement@enterpriseai.com
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Private deployment evaluation & MAP proposal

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week — our engineering and security teams were encouraged by Redwood's runtime and the on-prem options. We want to formalize an evaluation + mutual action plan (MAP) so we can get legal and procurement moving. High level ask: we need a 6–8 week POC (VPC-hosted pilot) that includes SOC2 evidence, KMS integration, and an on-prem licensing option for when we move to production.

Key timing: we want production-ready capability by end of July if possible; procurement would like commercial milestones in the MAP (pilot acceptance -> pilot to prod ramp -> 12-month commit) with pricing and any platform fee waivers tied to each milestone. Please include milestone-based discounts/credits and commit tiers in your MAP.

I've attached a one-page summary of what procurement will require (EA_MAP_Request.pdf). Can you send a draft MAP + preliminary commercial terms by EOD Tuesday so we can align internally?

Best,
Lina Gomez
Director, Cloud Platforms
Enterprise AI Corp

Attachment: EA_MAP_Request.pdf (summary of procurement asks)

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@enterpriseai.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 11:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Private deployment evaluation & MAP proposal

Lina — thanks for the clear brief and the timeline. We can absolutely put together a MAP that ties commercial milestones to acceptance gates. Draft attached (MAP_Draft_v1.xlsx) and a SOC2 checklist we've prepared for Private customers (SOC2-Checklist.pdf).

High-level MAP proposal (draft):
- Milestone A (Week 0–2): Kickoff, infra prep, KMS onboarding — deliverables: network IP whitelisting, initial KMS test keys. Commercial: no charge, Redwood provides SOC2 artifacts for security review.
- Milestone B (Week 3–6): VPC-hosted pilot (3–4 weeks) with performance SLA for pilot routes. Deliverable: pilot acceptance criteria (latency, throughput, regression checks). Commercial: Pilot discount: 50% off hosted API unit rates for pilot tokens.
- Milestone C (Week 7–12): Production ramp / on-prem licensing activation. Deliverable: production deployment runbook + SRE runbook. Commercial options:
  * Option 1 — 12-month capacity commit $500k/year: waive platform fee in year 1 and provide 15% unit-rate discount.
  * Option 2 — 12-month capacity commit $250k/year: credit platform fee by 50% in year 1 and provide 10% unit-rate discount.
  * Option 3 — No commit: on-prem license + platform fee applies (standard list).
- Milestone D (post-go-live): Quarterly business review, quality monitoring and automated regression alerts included.

Two clarifying questions: 1) Is procurement ok with capacity-commit billing (monthly invoicing against an annual spend), or do they require per-seat or per-instance licensing? 2) Are there specific legal terms around indemnity/data segregation we should expect for on-prem installs?

Next steps: we'll update the MAP with any procurement preferences and aim to send a version for your internal review by EOD Tuesday. Vivek will scope the onboarding runbook in parallel.

Thanks — attaching the draft documents now.

Regards,
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP_Draft_v1.xlsx, SOC2-Checklist.pdf

From: Tom Walker <tom.walker@enterpriseai.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@enterpriseai.com
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 08:32:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Private deployment evaluation & MAP proposal

Thanks Priyom — quick follow-ups from procurement/IT after reviewing the draft: 

1) Licensing model: procurement prefers capacity-commit (preferred) but needs a breakout showing how capacity maps to expected token volumes and concurrent requests (we'll share target QPS). Can you provide a short table mapping commit tiers to expected token throughput?

2) Pilot structure: we'd like a two-phase pilot: a short 2-week validation (security + smoke tests) followed by a 4-week workload pilot. Procurement will not sign a long-term commit until pilot acceptance.

3) Platform fee: procurement will consider a platform fee waiver only if there is an explicit ramp schedule and a minimum 12-month revenue commitment. We are open to the $250k tier but need a partial cap on platform fee liability in year 1.

4) Legal: please confirm Redwood's standard on-prem license terms (MSA + SOW) and whether DocuSign is ok for signature routing. I've attached our RFP summary with priorities.

On timelines, if we start infra prep this week, we can complete the two-phase pilot and be in a position to commit by mid-July. That would meet the production-by-end-of-July ask if the pilot goes smoothly.

Tom Walker
Director, Procurement
Enterprise AI Corp

Attachment: EA_RFP_Summary.docx

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 16:10:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Private deployment evaluation & MAP proposal (internal)

Team — read the thread from Tom/Lina. Good engagement; a few internal points before we send a revised MAP to Enterprise AI: 

- Commercials: I'm comfortable with the two commit tiers Priyom proposed but we should:
  * Cap the maximum platform fee liability in year 1 to protect Redwood (propose a $50k cap for EAC as a negotiation buffer).
  * Offer a phased credit schedule: 100% platform fee waiver at $500k commit, 50% credit at $250k commit.
- Legal / Licensing: ask Legal to prepare a modular on-prem license that enumerates platform fee, support SLAs, and a SOW template that maps to MAP milestones. No unusual indemnities without Legal signoff.
- Onboarding: Vivek, please prepare a 1-page SRE runbook focused on KMS and network steps and a realistic resource estimate for our professional services (hours & estimated cost).

Action items:
- Priyom: update MAP with Tom's two-phase pilot and add the commit-to-throughput table.
- Vivek: SRE runbook & estimated PS scoping by EOD Friday.
- Marissa: I'll loop Legal to draft MSA + SOW with platform fee cap language.

We should aim to have a customer-facing MAP and initial commercial term sheet ready before EOD Friday so procurement can review next week.

-Marissa
VP, Sales
Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 26 May 2026 14:55:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Private deployment evaluation & MAP proposal

Priyom / Marissa / Vivek — updating you after our internal sync. Procurement is prepared to proceed on the $250k commit path provided Redwood can: 1) provide the commit-to-throughput table, 2) commit to the phased pilot schedule (2-week validation + 4-week workload), and 3) include a platform fee liability cap in year 1. We prefer platform fee credit (50%) in year 1 over a full waiver at $250k.

We are comfortable with Redwood preparing the MSA + SOW and routing via DocuSign. Please send an updated MAP that includes the two-phase pilot, the commit tiers vs throughput table, a concise professional services estimate for the on-prem cutover, and the proposed platform fee cap (we'll review). If we get the updated package + DocuSign routing this week, procurement is ready to sign and target go-live after pilot close (late July).

Also requesting: a single-sheet commercial summary we can circulate with Finance (numbers only) and a HubSpot deal link so procurement can track approvals.

Thanks — looking forward to the update.

Best,
Lina Gomez
Director, Cloud Platforms
Enterprise AI Corp

Attachment: Signed_MAP_intro.pdf
